MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 3, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on June 3, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 31, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations—The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations are the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiators are Dennis Wilberg and Keith Rattay

City Council Minutes  1  June 3, 2013
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Liability Claims; Claimant: Ms. Miranda, Agency:
  City of Mission Viejo

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member
Schlicht returned to the dais at 6:08 p.m.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for item CS1, the Council received information and
gave direction to staff. For item CS2, the City Council provided direction but there was no
reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Newhart Middle School’s Robotic Team "Gears & Geeks" for Placing 3rd
  in the VEX World Robotics Competition at the Anaheim Convention Center Plus the
  Award of Excellence for the Overall Pilot Program Sponsored by VEX

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to teacher Eric Gosselin and
  student members of the Gears and Geeks team.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that the taxpayers thank Bob Breton and the Friends of the Library
for spending $9,000 to complete the preservation of the Mission Viejo historic files and for their
part in collecting $2 million prior to that. He also thanked Susan Sellers and the Friends of the
Mission Viejo Dog Park for beginning the effort to sell pavers to help fund the dog park.

Carole Weidler, M.V.: thanked the City for the excellent Memorial Day Ceremony and the
American Heroes banners that graced the Civic Center the week before. She expressed her
thanks to the Council for supporting the Relay for Life and she discussed her recent attendance at
Mission Viejo High School's performance of Fiddler on the Roof. Ms. Weidler stated that there
is no need to go beyond Mission Viejo to fancy theaters when there is the kind of talent that
exists in this City. Lastly, she thanked City Council for being careful, conscientious stewards of
the taxpayers' money.

The following discussed their positions with the City's crossing guard company, All City
Management Services, and expressed concern that their hours might be reduced from 4 hours to
3 hours per-day: Karen Siegfried, M.V. (presented a petition signed by over 400 residents in
support of maintaining the current crossing guard hours;) Lisa Harcrow, M.V.: Carrie Payne,
M.V.; and Adrianna Brady, M.V.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: referencing the contract for street sweeping services and the discussion at

City Council Minutes  2  June 3, 2013
 the last Council meeting, he expressed disappointment that staff added stipulations to the bid
documents which could shut out certain companies.

Erin Lannon, Sullivan Solar Power: announced that more than 15 residents have taken the pledge
to go solar with their company, thereby committing over 85,000 watts of clean renewable
energy. As a result of the positive response, Sullivan Solar will extend their program to Mission
Viejo residents through June 17, 2013.

F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: announced that there is a very significant event taking place
tomorrow regarding San Onofre. The meeting will be held at the San Diego County Board of
Supervisors chamber, beginning at 8:30 a.m. and will be broadcast via the Internet at
http://av4b.com/live/. Mr. Holtzman stated that there will be four notable speakers discussing the
lessons learned at Fukushima and the impending dangers at San Onofre.

Robert D. Breton, M.V.: stated that the tennis community is extremely grateful for the newly
improved Marguerite tennis center and he thanked Musco Electric for upgrading the lighting
from 6 to 9 light standards at no charge. Mr. Breton noted that he wrote a letter to Musco
thanking them for their commitment to excellence and he asked the Council to do the same.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 8, 10, 14, 16 and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Council Member Schlicht announced that she will be voting no on item 23 because she is
concerned that West Coast Arborists has charged the same price for 8 years, therefore the City
may be losing service. She stated that the tree inventory has decreased and the City may not be
getting the best value so she believes it is time to go out for competitive bid.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  June 3, 2013

City Council Minutes  8  June 3, 2013
 16. South Coast Air Quality Management District Funding for Electric Vehicle Charging
  Stations

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked if staff has done an analysis on the need for these charging
  stations.

  Mr. Rattay responded that there has been no analysis but the City does get requests from
  residents so that is the genesis for doing this.

  The Council Members asked questions and expressed an interest in seeing further
  information and/or studies on the matter.

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to table the item and
  direct staff to return with additional information.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the contract amount is going up, yet calls

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)

RECESS

At the hour of 8:44 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:56
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

33. Proposed 2013-15 Budget for the City of Mission Viejo

  Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that she is hoping the City will get going on the expansion of
  the cattery this year and she asked the Council for their support. She feels that the project is
  well worth it and is the next generation of improvements for the Animal Services Center.
  Mrs. Cody also reminded the Council that the DAWG Walk and Pet Faire will be held on
  Saturday, June 22 at the Village Green.

  City Manager Wilberg and Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented an
  overview of the proposed budget.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Council, as well as residents, should know what
  Mission Viejo is paying for Fire Authority services.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley responded that OCFA works for 23 cities and unincorporated areas.
  Fifteen cities are "structural fire fund cities" with fees taken directly from property tax bills.
  All property owners pay 1% in property tax and of that 1%, Mission Viejo pays 11% to
  OCFA. The other 8 cities are considered "cash contract cities" and the cost of their fire
  services is paid from the general fund.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

34. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that there is a new pet adoption shop in Mission Viejo
which gets its inventory from animal shelters. The shop rescues animals that are going to be
euthanized and he noted that they have other stores around the country and are doing well.

City Council Minutes  11  June 3, 2013
 Council Member Leckness also outlined his attendance at the Greg Louganis invitational diving
meet and last weekend's Relay for Life event.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at the City's Memorial Day ceremony and
she stated that it is very moving to remember the great sacrifices of those who have given us the
lifestyle that we maintain today. She encouraged her colleagues to look through the check
registers, especially the 4th quarter reports, to see where the money is being spent and to try and
find areas for savings. She cautioned that real estate property values have gone down and
property taxes lag behind. Historically, after a recession, property tax income will be less so she
recommended that the Council keep that in mind. Council Member Schlicht noted that she is
looking forward to studying the budget and she reminded residents to tune into the webcast on
SONGS on June 4 at 8:30 a.m. (http://av4b.com/live/.) Council Member Schlicht closed with a
quote from Dr. Samuel Johnson: "In order that all men may be taught to speak the truth, it is
necessary that all likewise should learn to hear it."

Council Member Ury

Mr. Ury stated that the Council Members are fortune enough to serve on a variety of Boards
throughout the county. In that context, they get to look at different yet similar data in terms of an
agency's finances. He feels that that Mission Viejo is definitely taking a look at the conservative
side of the budgetary projections. Council Member Ury noted that the Council has good
perspective and they have been conservative and, from that standpoint, he is very encouraged by
what he hears. Lastly, Council Member Ury stated that as City continues to increase its
budgetary reserves he wants to make sure that the Council is not worshiping those reserves. Part
of the challenge is to determine what programs should be reinstated or put in place and he
believes the Council would be remiss to put all of the budgetary savings back into reserves.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley echoed Council Member Schlicht’s comments about the Memorial Day
ceremony. She stated that the event seems to get better and better every year and she thanked
staff for doing an excellent job again. She also noted that the American Heroes banner display is
very moving and she is glad that the City is part of the program so the military heroes' names and
faces are out there for our residents to see. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined her attendance at the
El Toro Memorial Day ceremony and she thanked Mission Viejo resident Ziggy Wilczynski for
once again preparing a historical military display for that event. She also attended a recent mock
DUI crash at Capistrano Valley High School where students enacted an actual drunk driving
crash that killed two CVHS teens several years ago. This program is presented by Steve
Concialdi and Friends Against Drunk Driving (FADD) in conjunction with OCFA, OCSD,
Medix Ambulance Company, and Mission Hospital. The programs are held at most local high
schools every other year and she remarked that the enactments have a huge impact on the
students and most certainly help to save lives. City Clerk Hamman and MVTV staff also
attended the mock DUI crash and staff is looking into the possibility of featuring the program on
MVTV in the near future. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Steve Concialdi and all of the
agencies that support the program. She further outlined her attendance at the Relay for Life and
City Council Minutes  12  June 3, 2013
 stated that it was a wonderful event, as always. She noted that the Mission Viejo teams have
already reached their fundraising goals and money continues to come in. Mayor Pro Tem Kelly
reminded residents that there will be a blood drive on Friday, June 7 from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. and
those interested in donating can call her for an appointment or go to redcrossblood.org and use
the sponsor code COMV. Also, Carl Hankey School is having a pancake breakfast fundraiser on
Sunday, June 9 from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. to support their International Baccalaureate program.
And lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that Saddleback College is studying the need for a
new football stadium and the College's Foundation recently pledged to raise $500,000 for the
project. The stadium services the college, local high schools and could have the ability to host
CIF events. It will be a real asset to the City and she encouraged anyone with an interest in
donating or getting involved to please let her know.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that she and resident Diana Presta along with Crime Prevention
Specialist Tammy Descoteaux attended the Rotary Club Meeting on Tuesday, May 21 to discuss
the subject of prescription drug abuse and she noted that a lot of eyes were opened that day. She
also outlined her attendance, with Council Member Ury, at the ACC-OC Infrastructure
conference where they covered everything from transportation to homelessness and Obamacare.
She learned that the State is running a deficit of $300 billion in transportation funding which
equates to lack of maintenance for our roads. Mayor Reardon noted that there is a $5 million
annual county shortfall and the only reason that Orange County roads are in pretty good
condition is because of Measure M2 funding. She also announced that Caltrans is only working
on emergency-type projects however mobility projects are on hold. She stated that it was a big
eye-opener when she learned that transportation projects, in the future, will funded through toll
roads or taxes. Mayor Reardon outlined her attendance at the City's very memorable Memorial
Day ceremony and she and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also attended the El Toro Cemetery
ceremony. She expressed her partiality for the City's event and thanked staff for their tireless
work. Lastly, Mayor Reardon discussed her attendance at the outstanding Relay for Life and she
stated that everyone involved did a great job.

Council Member Leckness interjected that Mayor Reardon made an excellent observation at the
Relay for Life when she said" I made a list of all the people that I know that have died from
cancer. Then I made a list of all the people that I know who have fought and survived cancer and
the list of survivors was longer." Council Member Leckness stated that cancer is not a death
sentence anymore and that is what the Relay for Life event is all about.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:04 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 17, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.
